precepts.text: David brought the ark of the Lord and set it in the midst of the tabernacle that he had pitched for it in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.
precepts.why:
“And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.”

That is the history behind what Chronicles says: “the ark of God had David brought up from Kirjath–jearim to the place which David had prepared for it: for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem.” So in Solomon's day the ark was in the tent David pitched at Jerusalem, while the tabernacle Moses made in the wilderness stood at the high place in Gibeon, where Solomon and the congregation went.

precepts.text: David and the elders of Israel went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obededom with joy.
precepts.point: The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.
precepts.why:
“So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obed–edom with joy.”

That is the other account of the ark coming up to Jerusalem, the place David had prepared for it. Line up Second Samuel 6 and First Chronicles 15 and you have the history of how the ark came to be in Jerusalem before Solomon was strengthened in his kingdom.

precepts.text: Solomon said the Lord had made him king in the room of David his father, though he was but a little child that knew not how to go out or come in.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
First Kings 3 tells the same night, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and gives more detail of what was said. Solomon said: “And now, O Lord my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.”

That is what he meant in Chronicles: “Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people.” He knew he was not able to go out and come in before them on his own. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.

precepts.text: Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, that he might discern between good and bad.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
“Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?”

This is the same request as in Chronicles: “Give me now wisdom and knowledge … for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?” Kings shows what the wisdom was for: an understanding heart, to discern between good and bad, and to judge a people “like the dust of the earth in multitude.”

precepts.text: The speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.”

The Most High had said, “Ask what I shall give thee”, and Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge the people. That request pleased the Lord. Kings supplies this detail that Chronicles leaves out.

points: Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him exceedingly. The Most High established Solomon before he ever built the house.

Solomon spake to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every governor, the chief of the fathers, and went with all the congregation to the high place at Gibeon, where the tabernacle of the congregation that Moses had made in the wilderness was.

The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.

The brasen altar that Bezaleel the son of Uri had made was set before the tabernacle of the Lord, and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it. Solomon went up to that brasen altar before the Lord and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.

In that night the Most High appeared unto Solomon and said, Ask what I shall give thee. This same account is told in First Kings chapter 3, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; reading it there gives more detail of what was said.

Solomon answered that the Lord had shewed great mercy unto David his father and made him to reign in his stead, and asked that the promise unto David be established, for the Lord had made him king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude.

Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.

The Most High said to Solomon that because this was in his heart, and he had not asked riches, wealth, honor, the life of his enemies, nor long life, but wisdom and knowledge to judge the people, wisdom and knowledge were granted unto him.

The Lord also gave Solomon riches, wealth, and honor such as no king before him had, and none after him would have the like. When a man seeks the things of the Most High first, the other things are added unto him.

Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel. He gathered chariots and horsemen, having a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

The king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedars as the sycomore trees in the valley for abundance. Horses were brought out of Egypt, and the merchants received the linen yarn at a price and fetched up horses and chariots for all the kings of the Hittites and of Syria.
